claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To get started, I need to understand your family situation. Let me ask you a few questions.

**First, tell me about the child or children you're claiming for:**

1. **How old is the child?** (Or if you have multiple children, what are their ages?)
   - Under 16
   - 16-19 years old
   - 20 years old or over

Please provide the child's name(s) and age(s) so I can assess your eligibility properly.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 18 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're asking about **Alex, who is 18 years old and lives at home with you**.

Since Alex is 16-19 years old, I need to check some additional criteria to determine eligibility. The key question for this age group is whether they're in education or training.

**Is Alex currently:**
- In full-time education (such as A-levels, college, university, or other full-time study)?
- In an approved training course?
- Or is he working full-time or not in education/training?

This will help me determine the next steps in the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in college or anything like that. He finished school and he's just working at the moment, nothing full-time though - just a part-time job to earn a bit of money.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. So Alex has finished school, is not in education or training, and is working part-time.

Let me navigate through the assessment based on this information.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to clarify one more thing about when Alex finished school:

**When did Alex finish school?** Specifically:
- Did he leave school within the last 20 weeks (roughly the last 5 months)?
- Or was it longer ago than that?

This is important because there are special rules for young people who have recently left education.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, it was longer than that. He left school last year actually, so it's been well over 5 months now.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. Since Alex left school more than 20 weeks ago and is not currently in education or training, let me navigate to the next step.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the assessment, I have your eligibility outcome:

## **INELIGIBLE for Child Benefit**

**Reason:** Alex does not meet the qualifying conditions for Child Benefit.

**Why:** Child Benefit is only payable for:
- Children under 16, OR
- Young people aged 16-19 who are in approved full-time education or training

Since Alex is 18, no longer in education or training, and left school more than 20 weeks ago, he is no longer a "qualifying child" for Child Benefit purposes.

**Important note:** If Alex were to return to approved full-time education or training at any point, you could potentially claim Child Benefit again for him during that period.

Is there anything else I can help clarify about this decision, or do you have any other children you'd like me to check eligibility for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, I see. That's disappointing, but I understand. No, Alex is my only child, so I guess that's it then. Thanks for explaining it to me clearly though, I appreciate your help.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're welcome! I'm glad I could explain it clearly for you. I understand it's disappointing, but you now have a clear understanding of why Alex doesn't currently qualify.

Just to summarize for your records:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: If you have any other questions in the future about benefits or eligibility, feel free to reach out. Best of luck to you and Alex!
